## The question

In 2014 the Delta Cost Project's brief *Labor Intensive or Labor Expensive?* found that public colleges' hiring through 2012 had "largely mirrored rising enrollments" while private colleges added staff per student, mostly professionals rather than executives. This project rebuilds that brief from IPEDS, extends it through fiscal 2024 (staff trends to 2025), and asks what happened next. Public colleges reversed course: staff per student had been falling and began rising after 2012. Much of that rise comes from the denominator. Enrollment fell, mostly for reasons other than population, and staffing responded less than one for one. The rest comes from hiring aimed at attracting students: enrollment-facing staff, amenities and athletics.

## Posts

## Interactive tools

- [Overview](overview/index.qmd): the headline numbers by sector, and a guide to the tools.
- [Sector trends](sector-trends/index.qmd): faculty FTE, non-faculty FTE and other staff measures per 1,000 students, fiscal 1988 to 2025, with the replication of the 2014 brief.
- [Institution explorer](institution-explorer/index.qmd): any college's staffing, enrollment, spending by function and athletics against its sector.
- [Enrollment](enrollment/index.qmd): enrollment by sector and peer group, how much of the rise in staff per student is the denominator, online and dual enrollment.
- [State explorer](state-explorer/index.qmd): a state map of enrollment change, staffing and dual enrollment.
- [Population shocks](population-shocks/index.qmd): what population change predicted for enrollment, how staffing responds, and what explains the decline.
- [Who was hired](who-was-hired/index.qmd): occupation groups since 2015, enrollment-facing staff and coaches.
- [Amenities and athletics](amenities-athletics/index.qmd): amenity, academic and athletic spending per student, and whether any of it paid off in enrollment.

## Data and methods

All tools use public, aggregated data: IPEDS (NCES), NSF HERD, the Equity in Athletics Data Analysis (EADA), USA Today NCAA finances, BLS local-area unemployment and SEER county population estimates. Fiscal 2024 and 2025 IPEDS values are NCES provisional. Each tool's data folder has a [README](data/README.txt) listing every file, its source and its years.
